CVE-2026-111089.description:
Apache Wicket reads texts from the application's resource bundles — a localized label, a css class name — and writes some of them into the JavaScript and the markup it generates for a component. Those texts are placed inside single-quoted JavaScript string literals and inside quoted attribute values without being escaped for that context, so a text containing a quote ends the literal or the attribute, and what follows is parsed as script or as markup in the application's origin when the page loads.

A resource bundle entry is authored for the application and does not say where the framework will write it. The same key is read by the framework into element text, where Wicket escapes it, and into the contexts below, where it did not. A text containing an apostrophe, which is ordinary in several languages, is enough to break the page; a text under the influence of another party is enough to run script.

CVE-2026-99686.title: vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order
CVE-2026-99686.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order

vhost_add_used_n_in_order() advances start by nheads[i] but wraps it
with a single subtraction. If start + nheads[i] >= 2 * vq->num, start
can remain outside the ring.

With used-ring logging enabled, start > vq->num makes (vq->num - start)
underflow. log_write() then sets bits beyond the dirty-log bitmap,
potentially corrupting adjacent userspace memory. This is reachable on
the vhost-net TX path with VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER: done_idx can reach
VHOST_NET_BATCH (64), triggering the issue with a 32-entry ring.

Wrap start with a mask to keep it within the ring. VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM
enforces a nonzero power-of-two ring size, allowing start to be wrapped
using & (vq->num - 1).

CVE-2026-99732.title: mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock
CVE-2026-99732.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock

memory_failure() -> ... -> filemap_remove_folio() can read mapping->a_ops
after the inode has been freed. Once the folio is deleted from the
pagecache it no longer pins the mapping, so after i_lock is dropped
e.g., a concurrent final iput() can evict and free the inode before
filemap_free_folio() looks up mapping->a_ops->free_folio.

Most callers hold a reference on the inode, but not all.

Documentation/filesystems/vfs.rst explicitly states that ->free_folio()
must not assume the original address_space mapping still exists.

Fix it by loading ->free_folio while i_lock is still held, similar to
what folio_unmap_invalidate() does.

Inline filemap_free_folio() into its remaining caller such that
delete_from_page_cache_batch() also just loads the callback before
dropping the i_lock.

The bug was found by code inspection and has not been reproduced.

CVE-2026-9586.title: Unauthenticated SQL Injection Leading to Remote Code Execution in Switchvox SMB
CVE-2026-9586.description: An unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability exists in Sangoma Switchvox SMB Edition 8.3 (104997). The /pa endpoint processes XML content beginning with <PolycomIPPhone> and directly concatenates the user-controlled PhoneIP value into PostgreSQL queries without sanitization or parameterization. An unauthenticated remote attacker can execute arbitrary SQL statements against the backend PostgreSQL database using a single crafted request, including database operations and remote code execution.
